question: Can a correctly weighted fallible inspection report retain useful constraints without hard exclusion of the true history?
status: implementation and engineering validation before scientific admission
generation: A binary report of current inspection flips independently with probability one minus supplied reliability. A fixed uniform draw per world/case couples reliability levels and is shared by both fits. Current native/shift cases differ; only worlds are paired.
comparison: Apply all three treatments to the identical retained direct forecast and common supplied exact target support. Soft likelihood uses the supplied binary channel; hard masking treats the report as certain. If a hard report empties all support, retain the prior and count the explicit conflict.
headroom: Both source cells must bind their exact-law positive headroom and both validation-stopped fits before dispatch. No new learned architecture or method-by-support superiority claim.
stopping: Complete this finite reliability grid and its full frozen-source replay. No reliability tuning on development outcomes. Stop a hard-constraint recommendation for this noisy field if false records exclude truth; retain metric reversals and uncertainty.
validation: Certain soft report equals hard projection
False authoritative report retains positive true mass only under soft treatment
Full scientific frozen-source family replay before acceptance
transport: Twelve engineering false-context fixtures, six correct and six incorrect inspection reports at reliability 0.95/0.8/0.5, exercise the canonical ProcessCase and offline exporter read-only. Report truth and exact posterior remain evaluator-only; case IDs do not encode correctness.
limits: A stipulated independent binary witness is not ordinary semantic context
